name: @ao-mcp/local

tools.name: authenticate
tools.description: Add an Automated Operations account, organization, or role context. Opens the browser only when a reusable context is not already stored, then applies the new credential to THIS session immediately — no restart or reconnect. Call it when a tool returns error "auth_required" and no stored context works. Use `switch_account` for normal account or organization switching; pass switch_user=true here only to add another context. When a browser sign-in is needed it returns at once with a sign_in_url: show that link to the human (the browser the bridge opens may be the wrong one), then call this tool again to wait for the sign-in and apply it. Retry the original call after it succeeds.

switch_user.description: Add an account, organization, or role context that is not already stored, even if the current session is valid. To select an existing context without login, use switch_account instead.

open_browser.description: Open the system browser at the sign-in link. Set false when the human will open the returned sign_in_url themselves, e.g. because their default browser isn't the one they use AO in.

tools.name: auth_status
tools.description: Report whether this MCP session is signed in to Automated Operations, which credential source is in force (environment variable vs stored login), when it expires, and whether it can refresh itself. Cheap and read-only — call it before assuming a failure is an auth problem, or to tell the human who they are signed in as. The result also supplies the canonical runtime capability discovery and invocation workflow for clients that lazy-load tools.

tools.name: sign_out
tools.description: Clear the stored Automated Operations credential and drop it from this session. Use when the human asks to sign out or hand the machine to someone else (pass all=true to also forget every stored account in the switcher). Subsequent tool calls will fail with auth_required until `authenticate` is called.

all.description: Also forget every stored account (the account-switcher list), not just the active credential. Use when handing the machine to someone else.

tools.name: switch_account
tools.description: Switch this MCP session to a stored Automated Operations account, organization, and role context. Called without arguments it opens the client's native selector when elicitation is supported; otherwise it lists the choices for a follow-up call. A switch to a context other than the active one is always confirmed with the human first, so it cannot complete on clients without elicitation. Stored refreshable contexts switch without browser login. Use `authenticate` only to add a context that is not stored yet.

context_id.description: The stored account (profile) to switch to, from the list this tool returns when called without arguments. Omit to be shown the choices.

org_id.description: Organization ID from the available_contexts list. Pass with role_id to add that context; AO may require the human to pick it in a browser sign-in.

role_id.description: Agent role ID from the available_contexts list. Pass with org_id.

tools.name: local_agent_status
tools.description: Report the running local AO agent version and update state. Native installs update automatically in the background and activate on the next MCP process start; the npx distribution resolves the latest release before launch. Call when the user asks whether AO is current or an update notice says a client restart is required.

instructions:
Automated Operations MCP. This bridge started without a usable sign-in (not signed in on this machine), so it is not connected to Automated Operations yet. Remote tools appear once you sign in; until then every remote request fails with error auth_required. Call `authenticate` to sign in: it opens the user's browser and connects this same session, after which the bridge sends notifications/tools/list_changed (list the tools again if your client does not do so by itself). On a machine without a browser the human can run `ao-mcp-local login` in a terminal: the bridge picks that sign-in up by itself within a few seconds and connects this same session (calling `authenticate` afterwards also applies it, without a browser).

This connection runs through the local Automated Operations bridge, which serves these tools itself (they never leave your machine): `authenticate`, `auth_status`, `sign_out`, `switch_account`, `local_agent_status`.

Error contract: a failure caused by authentication comes back as a tool result with isError set and a JSON body {"error":"auth_required","detail":...,"action":...} (also in _meta."ao.auth"). It is ACTIONABLE, not fatal: follow `action` — normally call `authenticate`, which signs the user in via their browser and applies the new credential to this same session — then retry the original call. When it returns a `sign_in_url`, show the human that link to open in the browser they use AO in, then call `authenticate` again to finish. The human does not need to restart anything or run a terminal command. To change account, organization or role, use `switch_account`.

Runtime capability workflow: call `search_plugins`, then `describe_plugins` for exact schemas, then `plugin_query` for classified reads or `plugin_execute` for classified writes. Do not treat `describe_plugins` alone as the discovery entry point. Other AO tools (documentation, the event intake contract, host identity, integration guides) are reached with `find_tools` and `call_tool`.

If AO tools you used earlier stop appearing in your tool list, the server has not gone away: your role's tool set changed. `find_tools` and `call_tool` still reach every tool your role allows.

Large results: when a tool result is too big to return inline, it carries a `resource_link` to an `ao://results/<id>` URI (also in _meta."ao.resultResource", with its expiry in _meta."ao.resultExpiresAt"). Read the complete JSON with resources/read on that URI in this same MCP session — the link is bound to the session that produced it, expires 15 minutes after the call, and cannot be read from another session or after the bridge reconnects; re-run the tool to get a fresh one.
